title: language models’ hall of mirrors problem: why ai alignment requires peircean semiosis
core_idea: Examines limitations of large language models through Peircean semiotics, arguing that basic LLMs exist within a 'hall of mirrors'—reflecting only the linguistic surface of training data without indexical grounding or participation in socially-mediated epistemology—and considers how developments such as extended context windows, persistent memory, and mediated interactions relate to the prospect of AI systems functioning as Peircean interpretants, thereby reframing AI alignment as a problem of semiotic grounding.
tldr: Applies Peircean semiotics to LLMs to highlight their lack of indexical grounding ('hall of mirrors'), explores how new architectural and interactional features relate to semiotic interpretants, and reframes AI alignment as an epistemological and semiotic challenge.
